[[File:Hersh Moysés Nussenzveig.jpg|right|thumb|123px|Nussenzveig]]
'''Herch Moysés Nussenzveig''' (16 January 1933 – 5 November 2022) was a Brazilian physicist, professor at [[Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro]] and member of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] of [[Jewish]] Descent. He authored several textbooks, notably the collection ''Curso de Física Básica'' (''Course of Basic Physics''), winner of the [[Prêmio Jabuti]] in 1999 on the category ''Ciências Exatas, Tecnologia e Informática'' (Exact Sciences, Technology and Informatics).<ref name="cbl">{{cite web|url=http://www.cbl.org.br/jabuti/telas/edicoes-anteriores/premio-1999.aspx |title=Edições Anteriores - Prêmio 1999 |publisher=Câmara Brasileira do Livro |accessdate=12 April 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100910015958/http://cbl.org.br/jabuti/telas/edicoes-anteriores/premio-1999.aspx |archivedate=10 September 2010 }}</ref> He was president of the [[Brazilian Physical Society]] from 1981 to 1983.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sbfisica.org.br/v1/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=82&Itemid=227|title=Diretorias Anteriores da Sociedade Brasileira de Física|accessdate=7 February 2010|date=|archive-date=8 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101008090151/http://www.sbfisica.org.br/v1/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=82&Itemid=227|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Nussenzveig was born in [[São Paulo]] on 16 January 1933.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://abc.org.br/resultado.php3?codigo=nusse|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150328221314/http://abc.org.br/resultado.php3?codigo=nusse|archive-date = 28 March 2015|title = ABC – Academia Brasileira de Ciências}}</ref> He was a PhD student of [[Guido Beck]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/herch-moyses-nussenzveig-alem-do-arco-iris/|title=Herch Moysés Nussenzveig: Além do arco-íris|website=revistapesquisa.fapesp.br|accessdate=18 December 2022}}</ref> He was known, among other things, for explaining effects such as the [[glory (optical phenomenon)|glory]], an optical phenomenon.

In 1986, he was the recipient of the [[Max Born Award]]. The prize citation reads: "For distinguished and valuable contributions to the theory of [[Mie scattering]] and to the theories of the [[rainbow]] and the glory."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/maxborn/|title=Max Born Award - Awards - Optica.org &#124; Optica|accessdate=18 December 2022}}</ref>

His two brothers, wife, and three children are all scientists or physicians; one of his children is the mathematician [[Helena J. Nussenzveig Lopes]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/2010/07/18/herch-moys%C3%A9s-nussenzveig-al%C3%A9m-do-arco-%C3%ADris/|title=Herch Moysés Nussenzveig: Além do arco-íris|trans-title=Herch Moysés Nussenzveig: Over the rainbow|magazine=Revista Pesquisa|publisher=[[São Paulo Research Foundation]]|first=Ricardo|last=Zorzetto|date=July 2010|access-date=27 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228161548/http://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/2010/07/18/herch-moys%C3%A9s-nussenzveig-al%C3%A9m-do-arco-%C3%ADris/|archive-date=28 February 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nussenzveig died on 5 November 2022, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |title=Adeus a Herch Moysés Nussenzveig |url=https://ufrj.br/2022/11/adeus-a-herch-moyses-nussenzveig/ |access-date=5 November 2022 |publisher=UFRJ |date=5 November 2022}}</ref>
